what: Everpure, formerly Pure Storage, makes all-flash data storage systems and the software that runs them. It sells storage as a subscription service as well as equipment, and supplies large flash systems for AI training clusters.
customers: Large enterprises, cloud providers and AI infrastructure operators that need fast storage at scale.
money: Evergreen subscriptions, cloud storage and support
moat: Its own flash module design rather than off-the-shelf solid-state drives, which gives better density and efficiency, plus a subscription model that upgrades hardware without a rip-and-replace.
risks: Operating margin of about 3% is thin because of heavy stock-based compensation
Flash memory price increases raise its input costs
Large hyperscaler deals are lumpy and can distort quarters
opportunities: Revenue grew about 16% last year with a 70% gross margin
Analysts see about 35% upside from current levels
A design win with a major hyperscaler would be a large and long-lived revenue stream
watch: Subscription annual recurring revenue and hyperscaler deployment progress.
